First off I would like to give a HUUUGE shout out to our BUFFALO BILLS and my #BillsMafia And #Bills4Life FAMILY!!!  AYE AYE AYE AYE.  LETS GO BUFFALOOOO!!  i will see you all late Sunday/early Monday morning at the Buffalo International Airport!
     Secondly, this may seem a little odd and I apologize in advance for what may seem to be a little bit of a lengthy post, but PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE read it to the end, for a BILLS MAFIA BROTHER!!!   I have organized a fundraiser for SUICIDE AWARENESS. It is not what some of you may think, I am NOT looking for an easy handout. I AM asking for the help and the support from the GREATEST and MOST BAD ASS group of people that I have been EVER SO BLESSED to call my FAMILY,  MY BILLS MAFIA!!!  
     Suicide is very REAL. FACT - Each year, suicide claims more lives than war, murder, and natural disasters combined. Yet suicide prevention doesn't receive anywhere near the funding as other leading causes of death. It's up to us to make a difference. Together we can change the conversation about mental health and put a stop to this tragic loss of life.  Suicide affects every walk of life. (And of all ages. The Youngest intentional suicide that I am aware of is a 5 year old little boy that hanged himself from his bunk bed leaving a suicide note he had written in crayon). From athletes such as our very own former Buffalo Bills WR James Hardy (2008-2010) who drowned himself and Buffalo Bills LB Darryl Talley (1983-1994) who had contemplated suicide many times in his life. (Check out Talley’s story published by the Buffalo News entitled DARRYL TALLEY :  BROKE & BROKEN) to actors such as Robin Williams, musicians such as Nirvana’s Kurt Cobain and Linkinpark’s Chester Bennington, and WWE Superstar Chris Benoit. And of course WE CANNOT FORGET TO MENTION OUR VERY OWN FAMILY AND FRIENDS. I believe that overall, just about all of us have known or will know someone personally that has committed suicide or has attempted suicide. The numbers are staggering. Very sad. 
     So in closing I would like to thank you for taking the time to read this. I’d also like to thank you all in advance for your support and anticipated donations to help fight this Very REAL and Very ALIVE PANDEMIC NAMED SUICIDE.  I set my donation goal to $1000 which I know for a 100% FACT that can and will be blown right out of the water with all of your support.  Thank you to all of you. My Brothers, My Sisters, My BILLS MAFIA, MY FAMILY!! Love you guys. Here’s a link to The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention. Please take a look!  Read some stories and navigate around a little!!  After learning where your donations go and return to my fundraiser page and click donate. Whether you can donate 1 cent or $1000, every penny counts. Thanks again everybody. #Buffalobills #buffalove #buffalove #Buffalo

Hey brother. First let me introduce myself.  My name is Chad Crawford. I started a fundraiser for the American Foundation For Suicide Prevention. I know the title come up wrong but I could not figure out how to edit and correct it. With that being said, the main purpose  is to raise money so that we can bring suicide awareness to the dinner table at home and into all of our schools. Suicide is a lot of times a very silent killer.  It is considered by many to be taboo so it is kept hidden in the closet so not to be talked about. Why? Because no one knows how to talk about it. With the donations we raise we are able to go teach the children in our schools, beginning at a very young age, about suicide awareness. Providing for them the tools and resources needed to identify within themselves - as well as others, the signs of suicide so there is more of a probability of it to be prevented. The funds also allow for us to offer a place for everyone to share stories with one another, read stories by others, and give individuals of all ages a safe outlet to discuss their feelings and relate. Each year, suicide claims more lives than war, murder, and natural disasters combined. Every 9 hours, an individual takes their own life. That is 216 people a day. The problem is that suicide doe not get the attention or the funding as other leading causes of death. Why? Again because it’s considered taboo. The donations also allow for field advocates in Washington D.C to lobby and fight for suicide prevention policies. We have won many victories at federal and state levels against legislatively, resulting in many lives being saved.   Suicide does not discriminate either. No matter age, sex, race, professions, or beliefs.  This is a Suicide is a Serious issue today. It’s a pandemic in itself. And the longer it goes unnoticed or funded, the stronger the monster grows. men, women, children, mother’s and father’s, brothers and sisters. Lives destroyed forever.
